messages.subject: How do I implement a uniform prior for spatial precision in INLA?
parts:
I fitted a spatial model using the inbuilt prior for spatial precision and which to compare he result with a diffuse improper prior (e.g uniform prior sigma ~ U(0.001, 100)).
firstly I had to find the distribution for precision which is the inverse uniform distribution of sigma (since tau = 1/sigma) which is given as 
f(tau) = tau^(-2)*(b-a)^(-1). 
I then tried using the expression syntax to implement that in r-INLA as shown below, (which you can copy and paste into your R-console to verify what I am saying all things been equal)
 
y = rnorm(1)
a = 0.001
b = 100
uniprior = "expression;
a = 0.001;
b = 100
sigma = 1;
dens = sigma^-2*(1/(b-a));
return(dens);"
hyper.new = list(prec = list(prior = uniprior))
r.new = inla(y ~ 1, data = data.frame(y), control.family = list(hyper = hyper.new))

 
but I am having this error

b=100

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How do I implement a uniform prior for spatial precision in INLA?
parts:
Hi,

Do not use a semi-colon after ‘expression’ but a colon. Also, you can check here for more details about using expression:

https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/inla-gitbook/ch-priors.html#priors-defined-with-expression

This includes the implementation of a uniform (improper)  prior on the st. deviation. Remember that you need to compute the log-density of the prior and that the internal parameter must be unbounded.

Best,

Virgilio

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: How do I implement a uniform prior for spatial precision in INLA?
parts:
note that the 'expression:' should return the log(prior(theta)) where
theta is the internal parameterisation.

if

f(tau) = tau^-2

say, then with

theta = log(tau)

you need to do a change of variable to get

g(theta)

and then return

log(g(theta))

note that the varible 'theta' in the expression, should NOT be
initialised, as its initialised by the value of the log(prior) to be
evaluated for.

see the doc for 'expression:' for an example.

if unsure, do an 'expression:' for a standard prior and check that you
get the same result.

H

messages.author: daf6acb67d601fa2
messages.subject: Re: How do I implement a uniform prior for spatial precision in INLA?
parts: I tried the Gomez suggestion and came up with this

uniprior = "expression:
a = 0.001;
b = 100

log_dens = 0 - log(sigma*sigma) - log(b - a);
return(log_dens);"
which gives me the same (when compared to one I found in the link Gomez shared)  result when I plotted the marginal posterior fixed effect parameter and the and the marginal posterior for random effect variance
